sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Daily biology and biomedicine batch announced Monday, 2 November 2026; 10 papers highlighted. The strongest pattern is computational biology for regulatory-sequence design, model interpretation, and biochemical dynamics, alongside experimentally grounded small-molecule design and biomedical imaging. Agenda: start with sequence and molecule design, move through gene-network methods, then clinical imaging and prediction. arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking from an incomplete biomedical corpus, not a measure of readership or research validity.

sections.title: D2ML: Models for Direct-to-Biology Small Molecule Screening
sections.abstract: Assay-aware machine-learning models combine crude and purified direct-to-biology screening data and are used to select compounds for synthesis and testing.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors say joint modelling of multiple direct-to-biology assay stages improves predictions and can guide a potency–selectivity trade-off in their ROS1/TRKB program.
sections.unique_caveat: The study is limited to one 2,4-disubstituted pyrimidine core and a kinase program; the authors note small purified evaluation sets and call for testing broader chemistries and targets.

sections.title: Locality-Controlled Out-of-Distribution Guidance for Robust Regulatory DNA Sequence Design
sections.abstract: LOCOGEN uses a learned motif mask to apply diffusion-model guidance to background positions while protecting regulatory DNA motifs, balancing predicted activity, novelty, and sequence plausibility.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that localizing out-of-distribution damping reaches a balance of the three computational objectives that their tested baselines did not achieve.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper tests one masked diffusion backbone and relies on computational oracles; the authors state that generated sequences still need experimental validation.

sections.title: Co$^2$ODE: Conditionally Coarse-Grained Model Discovery for Rewiring in Biochemical Networks
sections.abstract: Co$^2$ODE combines context-specific selection of measured markers with a latent closure model to predict biochemical-network dynamics from single-cell phosphoproteomic data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose conditional coarse-graining as a way to expose context-dependent marker selection while retaining predictive performance.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors' own analysis finds that the data do not identify the underlying network structure: alternative marker selections and prior scores can fit equally well, and interventions are needed to distinguish them.

sections.title: Localizing predictive concepts encoded in neural representations via hierarchical testing
sections.abstract: CUTTIE hierarchically tests clusters of neural-network units to identify information-bearing groups and associate their representations with regulatory DNA motifs while controlling family-wise error.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a top-down conditional-independence testing method intended to localize model concepts with population-level error control.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a model-interpretation method evaluated computationally; motif correspondence does not establish that the model's features are causal regulators.

sections.title: Transmission and filtering of stochastic rhythms in bursty gene expression
sections.abstract: An analytical framework derives how degradation, transcriptional bursting, and variable upstream cycle timing shape the transmission of stochastic rhythms to gene expression.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author presents a quantitative theory for when upstream stochastic rhythms are retained or filtered by downstream gene-expression dynamics.
sections.unique_caveat: This is primarily theoretical work; the 10-protein comparison reuses prior experimental classifications rather than providing new experimental validation.

sections.title: GraphTFactor: A graph-based approach for proteins transcription factor prediction
sections.abstract: GraphTFactor encodes protein sequences as graphs and classifies transcription factors, with the authors reporting benchmark performance and interpretable sequence-region signals.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors say graph representations handle variable-length protein sequences without imposing a fixed sequence length and can support transcription-factor prediction.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not give dataset sizes or independent experimental validation; benchmark gains do not establish that predicted proteins function as transcription factors in cells.

sections.title: Quantitative Ultrasound Characterizes Perfusion Trajectories in Healthy and Inflamed Gingival Wound Healing
sections.abstract: A longitudinal ultrasound analysis estimates gingival perfusion after extraction and compares healing trajectories between visits classified as healthy or inflamed.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that velocity-weighted colour-pixel density tracked longitudinal perfusion changes and differed between healthy and inflamed recovery visits.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a small observational imaging cohort, not evidence that the measure improves treatment decisions or patient outcomes; the reported correlation with laser-speckle imaging was not statistically clear in inflamed visits.

sections.title: A General-Purpose Adaptable Foundation Model for Total-Body PET Kinetic Modelling
sections.abstract: LoRACM adapts a pretrained consistency model with low-rank updates to infer posterior distributions for total-body PET kinetic models across tracer, protocol, and modelling settings.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that LoRA adaptation can transfer a pretrained model to new PET kinetic settings with less than three hours of training on one A100 GPU.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not specify human cohort sizes; agreement with fitting baselines is not clinical validation or proof of improved patient care.

sections.title: Comparison of melanin subtypes using pump-probe microscopy
sections.abstract: Pump-probe microscopy and computational analyses characterize melanin photophysics across six lesion categories and test whether measured heterogeneity distinguishes tissue groups.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports that melanin heterogeneity differentiates cutaneous from non-cutaneous lesions in this dataset and that full transient-absorption curves classify most sampled subtypes above chance.
sections.unique_caveat: Heterogeneity was not correlated with malignancy in this dataset; this is an optical-characterization study, not a validated diagnostic test.

sections.title: Physiological Trajectories and Observation Patterns in ICU Mortality Prediction: Transportability Under Changing Measurement Conditions
sections.abstract: An ICU mortality-prediction study compares physiological trajectories with observation-frequency and timing features and tests performance under dataset transfer and changing measurement availability.
sections.claimed_contribution: The author reports that physiological summaries transfer more consistently than observation-pattern features, whose benefit changes with measurement timing and availability.
sections.unique_caveat: These are retrospective dataset results for prediction, not prospective clinical-utility evidence; the observation-pattern increment did not clearly transfer from the source system.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Sequence design and model interpretation: LOCOGEN and CUTTIE seek to make genomic models more biologically legible, but both remain computational studies. Learning biochemical and gene-expression dynamics: Co2ODE and the stochastic-rhythm paper formalize context-dependent signalling and noise transmission; predictive fit alone does not identify the true network. Assay- and imaging-aware biomedical modelling: D2ML uses assay-stage structure to guide measured compound synthesis, while ultrasound, PET, melanin, and ICU papers analyze human or tissue data through different imaging or prediction pipelines.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: LOCOGEN: test alternative diffusion backbones and perform wet-lab validation with synthesized sequences and matched MPRA assays across represented cell lines, keeping the evaluation oracle independent of guidance. Co2ODE: targeted perturbations that break correlated marker relationships, followed by held-out prediction and independent pathway assays, could test whether selected state markers are mechanistically informative. D2ML: expand prospective evaluation beyond one chemical core and kinase program, with larger purified-compound sets across targets. Medical imaging synthesis: multi-site repeatability and independent cohorts could assess ultrasound and melanin stability; for PET, the roadmap identifies noisy simulation expectations, gradient/adjoint computation, and simulation-budget allocation as open algorithmic challenges.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's clearest experimental signal is D2ML's model-guided synthesis and testing of new compounds. Sequence-design and network papers offer computational methods, but biological interpretation still depends on stronger intervention or wet-lab tests. Biomedical imaging and ICU results are promising measurements or retrospective analyses, not practice-changing evidence.
